newsitem.title: CANADA: TransCanada unaffected by Red River flood.
newsitem.headline: TransCanada unaffected by Red River flood.

text.p: TransCanada PipeLines Ltd has had no impact on its natural gas pipelines in the Canadian prairies or northern U.S. plains from severe flooding in the regions, the company said on Monday.

Residents of Emerson, Manitoba, a Canadian border town where TransCanada's pipeline system connects with two major U.S. pipelines, were being evacuated on Monday and Canada's military was helping to fortify dikes along the flooding Red River.
TransCanada has a major meter station about 10 km (6 miles) east of Emerson.
"I've double checked -- there are no problems (on the pipeline)," TransCanada spokesman Tony McCallum said.
The company's system interconnects with the Great Lakes Gas Transmission and Viking Gas Transmission systems at Emerson, about 161 km (100 miles) south of Winnipeg.
McCallum said he had heard of no operational problems on either Great Lakes, co-owned by TransCanada and Coastal Corp, or Viking, owned by Northern States Power Co.
The Red River, whose rising water has devasted vast regions of North Dakota, was expected to crest at Emerson on Wednesday.
Authorities said the U.S.- Canada border near Emerson would close at midnight (CDT) tonight and traffic would be diverted to northwest Ontario or western Manitoba.
